title: Volunteer overflow pool & hard-stop allocation policy for high-variance cycles
creator: Darren Lee
description:
Context:
We frequently see large variance in actual capacity during Q2 cycles due to hiring shifts, travel, and unplanned incidents. Current guidance (soft float & ad-hoc reassignments) causes inconsistent scope trimming and unfair load distribution. This ticket defines a lightweight operational policy: a volunteer overflow pool plus a ‘hard-stop allocation’ anchor that protects committed slices while providing a predictable place to put emergent or optional work.

Goals:
- Limit mid-cycle scope churn and last-minute decommits by providing an explicit overflow runway.
- Make scope cuts deterministic and equitable via a documented hard-stop allocation algorithm.
- Preserve velocity on committed features while enabling low-risk experiments and docs work to absorb bursts.
- Measure: reduce scope-change churn by 40% and reduce emergency reassignments by 50% in the pilot org.

High-level design:
1) Volunteer overflow pool: engineers opt into a named overflow roster at cycle start. Volunteers agree to be first responders for non-blocking tickets and small fixes. Volunteers are assigned a lightweight tag and paid time credit (1 point/month credit accounting) for surge contributions.
2) Hard-stop allocation anchor: for each initiative we reserve a hard-stop fraction (default 10% of staff-days) that is exclusively used as the trimming anchor if headcount drops or priority shifts occur. This prevents carving into the critical path of committed work.
3) On-ramp stages: new incoming tickets must land in one of three lanes (Core-Committed, Overflow, Greenfield). During week 0-2 the overflow lane accepts quick on-ramps; after week 2 only emergency patches go in.
4) Shadow capacity buffer: each engineering lead nominates one floating FTE equivalent to be shadowed (20% allocation) for cross-training; this is used as a temporary cover during short-term absences.

Trade-offs considered:
- Pro: Predictability for PM and PMM stakeholders; reduced firefighting for core squads.
- Con: Volunteer fatigue risk; complexity in tracking time-credit. We mitigate by rotating volunteers quarterly and automating credits in the capacity dashboard.
- Con: Teams may try to over-rely on overflow for deferred technical debt. Mitigation: explicit cost-of-deferral tag and quarterly review.

Pilot plan (next 6 weeks):
- Week A (Kickoff, 2026-02-22): Present runbook to Eng leads + release manager; collect volunteer rosters. Confluence doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/cycleops/volunteer-overflow-runbook
- Week B (Config + Dashboard): Engineering infra (ENG-8472) to add an overflow tag and time-credit field in the capacity dashboard. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/capacity-dashboard/pull/2345
- Week C–D (Trial): Apply policy to three cross-functional initiatives (Console Observability, Dedicated Autoscaling, Private Upgrade path). Measure incoming ticket flow into Overflow vs Core. Initial dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/internal/cycleops/overflow-pilot
- Week E (Assessment, 2026-03-12): Run a retro with participating leads; collect quantitative metrics and qualitative feedback.

Implementation notes & operational playbook links:
- Overflow opt-in template and pledge: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-overflow-pledge
- Automated crediting is planned as a minimal webhook from GitHub PR merger to the capacity dashboard; scope for ENG-8472.
- Hard-stop algorithm (simple deterministic): when actual capacity delta > 5%, trim from the initiative’s soft buffer up to the hard-stop fraction; if shortfall exceeds hard-stop, escalate to PM triage for cross-initiative rebalancing. Algorithm spec: https://confluence.internal.redwood/cycleops/hard-stop-algo-v1 (draft).

Progress updates (annotated):
- 2026-02-21 (Darren): Drafted proposal and shared with PM guild. Feedback: need clearer equity safeguards for volunteers.
- 2026-02-24 (Nora): Incorporated equity rotation schedule; added time-credit ledger column to dashboard mockups.
- 2026-03-01 (ENG-8472 owner, Priya Rao): Basic overflow tag implemented; webhook prototype in place. Blocking: capacity dashboard needs permission to consume webhook payloads.
- 2026-03-05 (Nora): Ran tabletop with Console team. Outcome: Console agreed to nominate 2 volunteers and reserve a 12% hard-stop for their initiative.
- 2026-03-09 (Darren): Collected pilot metrics: 18% of non-critical PRs routed to overflow lane; 2 emergency reassignments vs historical avg 5.
- 2026-03-12 (Review): Doc shared with Eng leadership; legal asked clarifying Qs about reward credit (HR has informal signoff path).

Open questions / blockers:
- HR/Comp signoff on time-credit vs comp implications (assigned to People Ops).
- Finalize dashboard automated crediting (ENG-8472 scope increase or separate ticket?).
- Should overflow volunteers require manager approval per person-week? Need to avoid overcommitting. Proposal: manager OK for first cycle, automatic renewal unless opted out.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Runbook published and linked in cycle kickoff template.
- Overflow tag and time-credit fields live in dashboard; webhook automation merges credits on PR close.
- Pilot metrics tracked for two cycles with >30% reduction in emergency reassignment frequency or a clear action plan to iterate.
- Retro with leads documented and rollout decision (scale/iterate/abandon) captured in Confluence.

Suggested follow-ups if pilot succeeds:
- Formalize volunteer rotation into quarterly staffing playbook (PM-ops doc).
- Add automated nudges in Slack on week-2 to close greenfield on-ramps.
- Evaluate small monetary stipend or extra PTO for high-contribution volunteers (People Ops consult).
